hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District fires 3 firefighters, suspends 2 others after hazing investigation
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will present the documented facts in that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

cards.headline: Waterspout, lightning strikes and fires hit Treasure Coast during Friday storms
cards.body:
Severe weather on Friday struck across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County, bringing waterspouts, lightning strikes and multiple fires to the region. Multiple residents sent videos to the WPTV newsroom showing a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian on Friday afternoon. Weather spotters in Port St. Lucie captured video of heavy rain moving through the area during the storm system.

Port St. Lucie resident Merry Moore O'Rourke reported more than 3 inches of rain in her rain gauge during the storm. The severe weather stretched into Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie experienced significant lightning activity throughout the storm, leading to multiple fire incidents in the area.

Lucie County Fire District crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening. Radar showed a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the house fire. The Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause of the house fire, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Moore O'Rourke described the intensity of the storm as it moved through her area. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She summed up what many across the region felt as the storms passed through. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District says 3 fired, 2 suspended after hazing investigation
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District says it terminated three employees and suspended two others following an independent investigation into allegations that senior personnel used a
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District says it terminated three employees and suspended two others following an independent investigation into allegations that senior personnel used a modified bug zapper to electrically shock junior firefighters while they were on duty.

The district released a statement Saturday, July 18, along with a 2025 workplace culture analysis and a May 2026 investigative report detailing the incidents.

According to the documents, firefighter-paramedic Roberto "Rocky" Tapia provided videos and photographs to district administrators in March 2026. Investigators determined that several of the recordings showed incidents that occurred at Station 1 in March and September 2024.

The device was reportedly constructed from a dismantled bug zapper and modified so it could deliver electrical shocks to people.

One video showed then-probationary employee and paramedic apprentice Matthew Lohse seated in a chair while senior employees asked him paramedic-related questions. Investigators said Lohse was shocked when he answered incorrectly as other employees watched and laughed.

Other videos showed then-probationary or apprentice firefighters Kyle Kirkham and John Edmondson being shocked multiple times. The report noted that the employees appeared to experience pain, including yelling, groaning, twitching and pulling away from the device.

Several witnesses told the investigator that the junior employees had consented to participating. Lohse, Kirkham and Edmondson also said they had agreed to be shocked.

However, independent investigator John "J.K." Keller concluded that the power imbalance between senior personnel and probationary employees undermined the credibility of those claims of consent.

The investigation found that only junior, probationary or apprentice employees were shown being subjected to repeated shocks. Investigators found no comparable evidence showing senior employees being seated, questioned and shocked for incorrect answers.

Keller concluded that Tapia, Kayla Gammie, Douglas Boudrias, Christopher Baldwin and Jordon Hutchison violated district rules governing employee conduct and workplace violence.

The report identified Boudrias, Baldwin and Hutchison as leading participants in the conduct and recommended that all three be terminated. Hutchison was also identified as the owner of the device and the person who modified it.

The investigator recommended 48-hour unpaid suspensions for Tapia and Gammie.

Tapia participated in the incidents and recorded the videos, according to the report, but investigators considered his decision to eventually report the behavior and provide evidence to be a mitigating factor.

The report found that Gammie participated in questioning Lohse while he faced being shocked for wrong answers but did not personally operate the device or help construct it. Investigators also noted that she accepted responsibility for her conduct.

The Fire District said it followed the independent investigator's recommendations, terminating three employees and suspending two.

## Earlier report raised concerns about station culture

The newly released documents also include a July 2025 workplace culture analysis of Station 1A conducted by attorney Susan Gainey.

That investigation did not substantiate formal harassment allegations or find specific policy violations. However, more than 30 employees were interviewed, and witnesses described the station as having a culture marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion, aggressive banter and behavior that sometimes crossed the line between horseplay and hazing.

Some employees reportedly described the station as cliquish and said newer personnel could feel isolated or unwelcome. The report also stated that firefighters had requested transfers, avoided bidding for assignments at the station or considered leaving the district because of the workplace environment.

Gainey recommended reassigning personnel, counseling supervisors and expanding training related to workplace conduct, leadership, conflict de-escalation and professional boundaries.

The Fire District said those personnel reassignments were operational and non-disciplinary because the allegations being examined at the time could not be substantiated through on-the-record testimony.

District administrators said the 2024 videos were concealed from management and did not become known until March 2026, resulting in a separate investigation.

Because some of the employees shown in the videos had previously accused Fire Chief Jeff Lee and District Attorney Kim Sabol of wrongdoing, the district said it hired outside counsel to avoid any appearance that the investigation was retaliatory or biased.

Keller recommended that the matter be reported to law enforcement and the Florida Department of Health in addition to the administrative investigation. The released documents do not state whether criminal charges were filed.

The disciplined employees have initiated the contractual grievance and arbitration process, according to the district. The Fire District said it will present its evidence during that process and does not plan to comment further while it remains pending.

The released materials did not include separate statements from the disciplined employees or their union.

cards.headline: Waterspout passes over Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian during severe weather outbreak
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian on Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom showed the waterspout moving through the area.

The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, and lightning strikes. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches of rain. The severe weather extended all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

Port St. Lucie experienced significant lightning activity that sparked fires. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. Radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the storm. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Moore O'Rourke described the experience as the storm moved through. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She added that the storm was radical and a little scary. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the region.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9.
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates and that air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time and that if they hung in there, it would have worked and built up pretty good. Dambeck said the Boston route is seeing great demand. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed and that JetBlue will evaluate continuously. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach.

cards.headline: E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks prompt diet changes across Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, prompting many people in the Treasure Coast to change what they eat.
cards.body:
The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: 2 in Palm Beach County, 2 in St. Lucie County and 1 in Martin County. Some families are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce. In downtown West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he's taking precautions while grabbing lunch with his father Brian on Clematis Street. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens said she bought two big bags of oranges, bread and some apples instead of produce, and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. She recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that can be peeled, including foods like bananas, melons and avocados. Barone's biggest warning is to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. Instead, she recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

cards.headline: Martin County teacher challenges school board authority in termination appeal
cards.teaser: A Martin County teacher is arguing the school board cannot reweigh evidence in her termination appeal.
cards.body:
The teacher contends the board lacks the authority to re-examine the factual evidence that led to her termination and must limit its review to procedural matters. The case involves a dispute over the scope of the school board's appellate authority when reviewing personnel decisions.

The appeal raises questions about how much deference school boards must give to initial findings in employee termination cases. The outcome could affect how future employment disputes are handled in the Martin County School District.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman claims $5 million scratch-off jackpot from Fort Pierce store
cards.teaser: Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County turned a $20 scratch-off into a $5 million jackpot.
cards.body: Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138. She purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90, while the chance of winning $5 million playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

cards.headline: Florida Rep. Angie Nixon gets September trial date for Capitol sit-in charges
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's Aug. 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman. Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter and pushed his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million, and her campaign promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup.

hero.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks 27-year-old mile world record in London
hero.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
hero.body:
Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company said Friday that this was the moment Josh Kerr stands to make history and bring the mile record home.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 in World Cup semifinal, advances to final against Spain
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit with two late goals to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina scored twice in the final moments to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday. Enzo Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute from outside the box, and substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time off a cross from Lionel Messi. England captain Harry Kane scored the opening goal in the 55th minute, but England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford and his defense could not hold the lead.

Argentina will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The defending champions have repeatedly fought back from difficult positions throughout the tournament. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved themselves after falling behind, showing collectiveness and brotherhood.

England has now lost in the World Cup semifinals three times, including defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm, while England held back with a feeling they had a lot to lose. Messi, now 39 and likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from further strengthening his case as the greatest soccer player of all time.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence decisions
cards.teaser: MLB made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent the use of artificial intelligence for in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started, to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies have prepared for two years to secure Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in New Jersey.
cards.body:
The final between Argentina and Spain will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel said the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Photographer's images of Messi bathing Yamal as baby resurface before World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photos taken in 2007 showing a teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal have become the most talked about images before Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took the photos in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Her baby boy was paired up with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

The photo went viral during the European Championship, but now with the World Cup final looming, interest in Monfort's photos has skyrocketed. Monfort said the fact that the final is in the U.S. has given it the extra push. He said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. Monfort, 58, said his loyalty is split between the 19-year-old Yamal and Messi, who is 20 years his senior. He has an everlasting love for the best player of all time, but said Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain, thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn national top 15 finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee, last month, qualifying the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a unit on the national stage after advancing through local, state, and regional competitions during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season. The team came close to a perfect score at nationals, recording a 9.9. Lazuka said it is hard to get a perfect 10.

Each gymnast described different motivations for entering the sport. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics but the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan pointed to all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube, noting how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. Looking ahead to the Junior Olympics, Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described feeling happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to children at Treasure Coast area sites
hero.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is providing thousands of free meals to children this summer through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program. The nonprofit organization supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer. Food Bank leaders emphasized that hunger does not take a summer break while highlighting the need for continued support during the summer months.

Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg provided viewers with a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen during a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV. The kitchen serves as the central hub where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, the organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out.

The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed. Food Bank leaders said the meals are distributed through partner locations across Palm Beach County to help families facing food insecurity during the summer. During the broadcast, viewers got a close look at the large-scale kitchen operation responsible for preparing meals daily. Chef Doug Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County.

The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season. Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

hero.headline: South Florida residents abandon salads as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread across state
hero.body:
Thousands of people across South Florida are changing their diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated produce continue to spread. The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The latest concerns center around lettuce linked to the outbreaks, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the country have been affected by the contaminated produce outbreaks.

Families across the region are avoiding leafy greens entirely. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are staying away from lettuce. Jenny Rhodes said she misses salads and berries but believes it is better to be careful. George Lorenz said he has heard about the outbreak and is trying to avoid contaminated produce. While grabbing lunch with his father Brian on Clematis Street in downtown West Palm Beach, Lorenz opted for pizza. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens bought two big bags of oranges, bread, and apples instead of greens and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, recommended consumers focus on produce with protective outer layers. She said it is not an excuse to abandon fruits and vegetables for donuts and that people should remain healthy. Barone advised people to stick to melons and foods with harder skins that can be peeled, including bananas and avocados. However, she warned that consumers still need to wash these items before cutting into them and peeling them. She said consumers should wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and suggested beans and nuts as safe alternatives that provide fiber and protein.

Barone issued a specific warning against bagged lettuce. She recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also advised avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. Barone recommended cleaning produce using a one-to-three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking and massaging the produce. She also advised cooking vegetables when possible. The outbreaks stem from contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Brian Lorenz said he is not avoiding anything but is making sure to wash food properly.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District fires 3 firefighters, suspends 2 others after hazing investigation
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will present the documented facts in that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District says 3 fired, 2 suspended after hazing investigation
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District says it terminated three employees and suspended two others following an independent investigation into allegations that senior personnel used a
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District says it terminated three employees and suspended two others following an independent investigation into allegations that senior personnel used a modified bug zapper to electrically shock junior firefighters while they were on duty.

The district released a statement Saturday, July 18, along with a 2025 workplace culture analysis and a May 2026 investigative report detailing the incidents.

According to the documents, firefighter-paramedic Roberto "Rocky" Tapia provided videos and photographs to district administrators in March 2026. Investigators determined that several of the recordings showed incidents that occurred at Station 1 in March and September 2024.

The device was reportedly constructed from a dismantled bug zapper and modified so it could deliver electrical shocks to people.

One video showed then-probationary employee and paramedic apprentice Matthew Lohse seated in a chair while senior employees asked him paramedic-related questions. Investigators said Lohse was shocked when he answered incorrectly as other employees watched and laughed.

Other videos showed then-probationary or apprentice firefighters Kyle Kirkham and John Edmondson being shocked multiple times. The report noted that the employees appeared to experience pain, including yelling, groaning, twitching and pulling away from the device.

Several witnesses told the investigator that the junior employees had consented to participating. Lohse, Kirkham and Edmondson also said they had agreed to be shocked.

However, independent investigator John "J.K." Keller concluded that the power imbalance between senior personnel and probationary employees undermined the credibility of those claims of consent.

The investigation found that only junior, probationary or apprentice employees were shown being subjected to repeated shocks. Investigators found no comparable evidence showing senior employees being seated, questioned and shocked for incorrect answers.

Keller concluded that Tapia, Kayla Gammie, Douglas Boudrias, Christopher Baldwin and Jordon Hutchison violated district rules governing employee conduct and workplace violence.

The report identified Boudrias, Baldwin and Hutchison as leading participants in the conduct and recommended that all three be terminated. Hutchison was also identified as the owner of the device and the person who modified it.

The investigator recommended 48-hour unpaid suspensions for Tapia and Gammie.

Tapia participated in the incidents and recorded the videos, according to the report, but investigators considered his decision to eventually report the behavior and provide evidence to be a mitigating factor.

The report found that Gammie participated in questioning Lohse while he faced being shocked for wrong answers but did not personally operate the device or help construct it. Investigators also noted that she accepted responsibility for her conduct.

The Fire District said it followed the independent investigator's recommendations, terminating three employees and suspending two.

## Earlier report raised concerns about station culture

The newly released documents also include a July 2025 workplace culture analysis of Station 1A conducted by attorney Susan Gainey.

That investigation did not substantiate formal harassment allegations or find specific policy violations. However, more than 30 employees were interviewed, and witnesses described the station as having a culture marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion, aggressive banter and behavior that sometimes crossed the line between horseplay and hazing.

Some employees reportedly described the station as cliquish and said newer personnel could feel isolated or unwelcome. The report also stated that firefighters had requested transfers, avoided bidding for assignments at the station or considered leaving the district because of the workplace environment.

Gainey recommended reassigning personnel, counseling supervisors and expanding training related to workplace conduct, leadership, conflict de-escalation and professional boundaries.

The Fire District said those personnel reassignments were operational and non-disciplinary because the allegations being examined at the time could not be substantiated through on-the-record testimony.

District administrators said the 2024 videos were concealed from management and did not become known until March 2026, resulting in a separate investigation.

Because some of the employees shown in the videos had previously accused Fire Chief Jeff Lee and District Attorney Kim Sabol of wrongdoing, the district said it hired outside counsel to avoid any appearance that the investigation was retaliatory or biased.

Keller recommended that the matter be reported to law enforcement and the Florida Department of Health in addition to the administrative investigation. The released documents do not state whether criminal charges were filed.

The disciplined employees have initiated the contractual grievance and arbitration process, according to the district. The Fire District said it will present its evidence during that process and does not plan to comment further while it remains pending.

The released materials did not include separate statements from the disciplined employees or their union.

hero.headline: Waterspout passes over Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian during severe weather outbreak
hero.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian on Friday afternoon as severe weather battered the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom showed the waterspout moving through the area.

The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, and lightning strikes. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches of rain. The severe weather extended all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

Port St. Lucie experienced significant lightning activity that sparked fires. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. Radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the storm. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Moore O'Rourke described the experience as the storm moved through. "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen," Moore O'Rourke said. She added that the storm was radical and a little scary. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the region.
